articles.title: Cuban Man in Miami Faces Charges for Filming Walmart Employee in Bathroom
articles.description: A 28-year-old Cuban national was taken into custody on Monday in southwest Miami-Dade, accused of taking photos and recording video of a Walmart employee inside a bathroom stall, as reported by the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office. The suspect, identified as Oscar Chamizo Martin, was caught around 12:15 p.m. at the store located at 14325 SW 268th St., in the Homestead area. He allegedly extended an orange-cased iPhone over the stall occupied by the victim. The Walmart employee noticed the device and, upon exiting the bathroom, confronted Chamizo Martin, who was the only individual present in that section at the time. Security cameras inside the Walmart recorded the employee leaving the restroom visibly distressed while calling for his manager. After the incident, Chamizo Martin left the store, but a sheriff's deputy contacted his employer and convinced him to return. Back at Walmart, the suspect denied taking any images, claiming someone else was responsible. However, he was found with an orange-cased iPhone that matched the victim's description exactly. Confronted with this evidence, he was arrested and taken to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center (TGK), one of the main jail facilities in the county. As of Tuesday, Chamizo Martin remained detained with a $2,500 bond for the charge of digital voyeurism and also faced an immigration hold that could lead to deportation proceedings. In Florida, digital voyeurism is classified under statute 810.145, which prohibits the use of imaging devices to secretly record individuals in spaces where they have a reasonable expectation of privacy, like bathrooms or dressing rooms. For individuals over 19, the offense is considered a third-degree felony, punishable by up to five years in prison. This is not the first time Cuban nationals in Miami have faced serious criminal charges related to such behavior, amidst intensified cooperation between county authorities and federal immigration agencies. Florida has seen a series of voyeurism arrests in Walmart stores throughout 2025 and 2026 across various counties, including a recent case in Ocala just two days prior, where another man was apprehended for allegedly secretly recording minors in a similar setting. The immigration hold on Chamizo Martin indicates that immigration authorities have been notified of his arrest, which may result in additional consequences beyond the ongoing criminal proceedings.

articles.title: Former Orange County church employee sentenced to 40 years for secretly recording children using spyware
articles.description: Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A California man who previously worked for an Orange County church was sentenced to 40 years in prison for using spyware to secretly record children and directing juvenile victims to produce child sexual abuse material. Jacob Melvin Hart, 46, of San Juan Capistrano, had pleaded guilty to attempted production of visual depictions involving sexual exploitation of a minor and transportation of visual depictions involving the sexual exploitation of minors, the U.S. Attorney's Office said. An investigation revealed that Hart had previously worked as an IT consultant for Crossline Community Church in Laguna Hills, where he had access to children, prosecutors said. He also managed the church's audiovisual and computer technology operations. Hart provided laptops equipped with spyware to several children at the church, allowing him to remotely activate the computers' cameras without the children's knowledge. Using the spyware, he secretly recorded at least eight children and possessed sexually explicit depictions of those children, prosecutors said. In June 2025, while returning from a mission trip to Haiti, Hart was arrested at Miami International Airport by U.S. Customs and Border Protection. An inspection of his electronic devices revealed an extensive collection of child sexual abuse material, including images and videos that he had directed children in Russia to create. On July 29, 2026, Hart was sentenced to 40 years in prison. Federal prosecutors said that in 2006, Hart was convicted in Oregon of invasion of privacy after secretly installing a hidden camera in a girls' locker room at a Christian children's camp. In January 2026, two alleged victims filed separate lawsuits against Crossline, accusing the church of negligence, after they were allegedly recorded by the refurbished computers given to them by Hart, the Orange County Register reported. One of the female victims said that in 2013, she needed a new computer at the start of a school year. Hart reportedly offered to give her a refurbished model, which the family accepted. Investigators said Hart had installed software enabling the girl's computer to be remotely accessed and monitored, according to the suit. The computer captured images of the girl nude in the bathtub and getting in and out of the shower. Another female victim said Hart gave her a computer in 2023 so she could assist with editing videos for the church. The computer later recorded the girl showering and getting dressed, her lawsuit said. The suits claimed that multiple children accepted a laptop computer from Hart, with the church's knowledge. Lawyers also alleged that church officials were aware of Hart's previous conviction in Oregon when they hired him in 2012, claiming he had disclosed his conviction and a pornography addiction to his new bosses, the O.C. Register reported. Several church staff members have since resigned following the lawsuits. Church representatives said they are cooperating with law enforcement on the investigation. In a statement to the Register, church officials said, "The Elders of Crossline Community church are deeply grieved by the actions of Jacob Hart and the pain and suffering he has caused, especially to the victims. We have provided regular updates to the church, launched an independent investigation and strengthened our internal safety protocols, volunteer screenings and hiring processes." "This defendant weaponized technology and abused positions of trust to invade children's most private spaces and sexually exploit them," said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones. "The 40-year sentence imposed on Jacob Melvin Hart means he will likely spend the rest of his life in federal prison. It protects children from a calculated predator and demonstrates that we will pursue those who produce and solicit child sexual abuse material, whether their victims are here at home or across the world." pendingReview.title: My Friend Wishes We Had Warned Her About Her Last Boyfriend. Well, I Have Some Unfortunate Intel on Her New One.
pendingReview.description: Sign up for the Slatest to get the most insightful analysis, criticism, and advice out there, delivered to your inbox daily. Dear Prudence is Slate's advice column. Submit questions here. Dear Prudence, My friend "Hannah" has been single for a long time, has dated various men over the years, and her most recent relationship ended very badly and hurt her a lot. After it ended, several friends spoke up about what they knew about her ex, and she was upset no one had warned her. Now she is dating again, and I found out someone she has been seeing is the ex of someone I know and have heard a lot about that is not good -- think unhinged behavior, threats, cheating, stalking, manipulating, etc. I'm worried Hannah will get hurt again, although so far this guy has been nothing but appropriate, charming, and fun with her. My gut says this could be love bombing, and I think Hannah isn't very good at noticing red flags until it's way too late (she tends to overlook a lot and get hurt months down the road after she becomes more invested). Should I tell her what I've been told about him? I am hesitant because it is hearsay from his last ex through a third person close to her (whom I trust to be truthful), and it also feels like I might risk my friendship with Hannah by saying these things about the man she is dating. On the other hand, if even half these things are true about him, she is walking into another bad relationship that will end in her getting hurt again. What should I do? -- Again and Again Dear Again and Again, Tell her. But deliver the news very gently, with a lot of disclaimers and caveats and -- this is key -- have very low expectations for what she will do with the information. Decide beforehand that after you share what you know, you will wash your hands of the situation and allow Hannah to make whatever choice she's going to make about her relationship, even if it's clear that it's one that will lead to suffering for her. Here's how that warning could sound: "Hey Hannah. I wanted to talk to you about something I debated whether I should even bring up to you. But I ultimately decided it would be best for you to have all the information so you could make the best decision for yourself. A friend of mine once dated Wayne and said some concerning things about him. She talked about threats, cheating, stalking, manipulation, and stuff like that. It made me really worried for you, and I remembered how you'd wished people would have told you what they knew about your ex, and that's why I am bringing the information to you. I know you've had a different experience with him, and I have no way of knowing whether what I heard is true, but I just thought it would be best for you to know so you can make your own decision." If she's concerned and intrigued, offer to put her in touch with the friend who said these things. If she bristles and becomes defensive, say, "I'm sorry if it was a misstep to bring this to you. I did it because I care and thought you would want to know, but I apologize for making the wrong call. We never have to talk about it again." Dear Prudence, My cousin "Nathan" and I have always had a good relationship despite a fairly large age gap (I'm 36, he's 51) because our moms were very close sisters. Nathan has long had a practice of posting long essays on his social media about family, gratitude, recent travels, his faith, his children, etc. I've always enjoyed reading his thoughts and found it quite charming that he could be so earnest with his self-expression in a time when a lot of people are pulling back what they share online. Recently, though, he has turned to publishing very obvious AI writing. It makes me so sad to see AI slop that sounds like travel brochure copywriting in place of what normally would have been a tender missive about spending time with his wife in a new city. Both of our moms passed away last year, and he has posted several long tributes to them that just ring so hollow and uncanny. I miss my aunt and my mom very much, and I know firsthand that grief is a strange process -- but it makes me feel weird to see them rendered in a classic AI cadence and tone. My mom and auntie were not "quietly" doing anything, but that's a chatbot's favorite phrase! I'm not mad at him for this. I just want to let him know I miss his old writing. I know he has it in him, and that AI isn't unlocking some previously inaccessible well of self-expression. He doesn't have a following other than his real-life social circle, and social media isn't his job. He's just always been an emotional, expressive guy ready to share an upbeat, philosophical take on a fairly benign subject, and I loved it! Do you think it's rude to give Nathan feedback that it's obvious he's using AI and also that it's not having the same effect as his previous writing? -- Concerned Cousin Dear Concerned Cousin, I can't be objective here because I have an outsized, unreasonably enraged reaction when people use AI to write and think nobody will notice. I don't know why it drives me nuts! Maybe because we can learn so much about people through their tone and their choice of words, and if everyone sounds like an AI bot, I don't see the point of even writing anything. Or perhaps I'm just resentful that many people aren't valuing writing, the one thing I think I'm good at, as much anymore because they are happy (thrilled, even!) with whatever slop comes out in response to their prompts. Anyway, I completely understand how you feel. The sad truth is that I'm pretty sure a lot of the public can't tell the difference between an essay by a human and an essay by a chatbot. So maybe this strategy is working for Nathan. He's getting his message (or a message that approximates his, but includes things like "my trip to Mexico wasn't just adventurous, it was incandescent" and "this salad is a quiet but impactful addition to my weekday dinners") across and probably receiving similar feedback. Who knows, maybe he has freed up some time to spend with his kids or pets or to actually do the cooking. So join me in privately seething and save your feedback until he explicitly asks for it. Prudie Wants to Hear From You! Readers often have great suggestions for our letter writers, occasionally disagree with a point Prudie makes, or simply want to provide some additional advice. Each week, Prudie will be replying to some of these comments and suggestions from readers, which will be featured on the site on Fridays for Slate Plus members. Write to us! Or submit a question here. Dear Prudence, A friend of my husband's has a nasty habit: Whenever he talks to someone, he invariably sprays them with spit. He doesn't have any medical issues or speech impediments that would cause it. It's just the way he talks. Obviously, it's gross and unsanitary. What would be an appropriate way of pointing this out to him so I don't get soaked every time we interact? -- Preparing to Invest in a Splash Guard Dear Preparing to Invest in a Splash Guard, Given that the vast majority of people do not get other people wet when they talk, I wouldn't be so fast to assume that there isn't a physiological issue behind what's going on with this guy. He might just not be vocal about it. Certainly he's not doing this spraying on purpose. Of course, that doesn't change your desire to protect yourself from a saliva shower. Try: "Oops, we must be standing too close together; I got a little spit sprinkle. Let me scoot back." Classic Prudie My co-workers and I have all been victims of a lunch thief over the last couple of months. We've tried putting notes and signs on our lunches asking people to please leave them alone, we've spiked our lunches with hot sauce or pepper in an attempt to make them unappealing (which also leaves them inedible for us), but the lunch thief has still been striking a couple of times a week. This was brought up at our last company-wide meeting, with dire consequences promised if it doesn't stop. After having his lunch stolen three times in one week, one of my co-workers installed a hidden camera in our break room...

pendingReview.title: Spain: British Couple Finds Hidden Camera Pointed at Bed During Wedding Anniversary Trip; Airbnb Suspends Listing
pendingReview.description: A British couple's 39th wedding anniversary trip to Madrid was cut short after they discovered a hidden camera in their Airbnb accommodation allegedly positioned directly toward their bed. Donna Nunn, 62, and her husband Raymond Nunn, 87, said they had already spent a night in the apartment before noticing the device. Airbnb subsequently refunded their stay and rebooking costs and suspended the property while investigating the incident, NDTV reported. Camera Discovered in Bedroom The couple arrived at the apartment in Madrid's Lavapiés neighbourhood on August 3. Shortly after arriving, they noticed a device in the living room that appeared to be a motion sensor or security camera facing the front door. Because the device showed no flashing light, they did not initially suspect that it was recording. The following day, while Donna was out sightseeing, Raymond noticed another device in the bedroom. Donna said the approximately four-inch device had a green light and was positioned in a corner facing the bed. Spain To Replace Ambassador to India Juan Antonio March Pujol Amid Financial Favour Allegations. Couple Leaves Property The discovery alarmed the couple, who said they were particularly distressed because they had already slept in the room without knowing about the device. They contacted Airbnb on August 4 and were advised to leave the property immediately. However, it was around 8pm by then, leaving the couple with limited options for accommodation that night. They eventually found another apartment roughly two hours south of Madrid and left the Airbnb on August 5, just two days after arriving. The incident also disrupted their plans to explore Madrid during their anniversary holiday. Spain Says 49,000 Migrants Crossed From Morocco Into Ceuta in a Single Day, 19 Bodies Recovered. Airbnb Suspends Listing Airbnb said it had issued the couple a full refund, including the cost associated with rebooking their accommodation. The company has also suspended the property listing while it investigates the report. Airbnb said it takes reports involving guest safety and privacy seriously. The company noted that it banned indoor security cameras in its listings in 2024, regardless of whether the devices are disclosed or switched off during a guest's stay. Airbnb said violations of its camera policy can result in action including the removal of listings and users from the platform. Privacy Concerns for Short-Term Rentals The incident has renewed concerns about privacy in short-term rental properties, particularly where surveillance devices may be concealed or improperly installed. Airbnb's current policy prohibits indoor security cameras, but the company says it investigates reports of violations on a case-by-case basis. For the British couple, the discovery brought an early end to what had been planned as a special anniversary trip. The investigation into the property and the device remains ongoing. (The above story first appeared on LatestLY on Aug 13, 2026 10:38 AM IST. For more news and updates on politics, world, sports, entertainment and lifestyle, log on to our website latestly.com).
